extracted.intended_audience: HHS agencies, HHS grant applicants and recipients, and grant administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Interim final rule adopting OMB's Uniform Guidance (2 CFR part 200) into HHS regulations (2 CFR part 300) and specifying HHS-specific additions, exceptions, and procedures for federal awards administered by HHS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption of 2 CFR part 200
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department of Health and Human Services adopts the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Guidance in 2 CFR part 200 and codifies the text, with HHS-specific amendments in 45 CFR part 75 and specified provisions of 2 CFR part 200, giving regulatory effect to the OMB guidance and supplementing it as needed for the Department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically adopts §§ 200.1 (definitions of MTDC, Equipment, and Supplies), 200.313(e), 200.314(a), 200.320, 200.333, 200.344, 200.414(f), and 200.501; part 300 gives regulatory effect and supplements OMB guidance for HHS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest policy requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS agencies' conflict of interest policies must address conditions under which outside activities, relationships, or financial interests are proper or improper; provide for advance notification of outside activities, relationships, or financial interests and a process of review; and outline how financial conflicts of interest may be addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition to 2 CFR 200.112, agencies with Public Health Service (PHS) funded research must ensure conflict-of-interest policies are aligned with 42 CFR part 50, subpart F.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition against profit for for-profit recipients
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for awards under SBIR and STTR programs, no HHS funds may be paid as profit to any recipient; 'profit' is any amount in excess of allowable direct and indirect costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an additional provision for for-profit recipients and is in addition to or an exception from other provisions of the part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of program income by for-profit organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for grants for research, program income earned by a for-profit organization may not be used to further eligible project or program objectives except in the SBIR and STTR programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research grants are an exception; otherwise program income restrictions apply to for-profits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit options for for-profit organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: For-profit organizations that receive awards have two audit options: (i) a financial related audit of a particular award in accordance with GAGAS (or of all awards if multiple HHS programs), or (ii) an audit that meets the requirements of 2 CFR 200, subpart F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For-profit organizations with annual awards totaling less than the audit threshold in subpart F are exempt from HHS audit requirements for that year, but records must be available for review by appropriate Federal officials or the GAO (see §200.501).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inapplicability of §200.315(e) to for-profit organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of §200.315(e) do not apply to for-profit organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is stated as an explicit applicability exception in §300.218(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility of Federal agencies for awards
rubrics_metrics.description: An HHS agency must have explicit statutory authority that makes Federal agencies eligible for awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a prerequisite for making Federal agencies recipients under HHS awards (§300.219(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Program income requirements for Federal entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for grants for research, any program income earned by a Federal institution must be used under the deduction alternative; any program income earned after the period of performance should be returned to the United States Treasury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit deviation for Federal entities receiving HHS awards (§300.219(b)(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Salaries and fringe benefits for Federal employees
rubrics_metrics.description: No salary or fringe benefit payments may be made from HHS agency funds to support career, career-conditional, or other Federal employees without permanent appointments at a Federal institution receiving an award; salary costs for Federal employees participating in official capacity are not allowable costs under an HHS award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recipient must allow the level of effort as part of each individual's official duties, but HHS funds cannot pay salary/fringe for such Federal employees (§300.219(b)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: No reimbursement of indirect costs to Federal agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal agencies may not be reimbursed for indirect costs under Federal awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit limitation for Federal entities (§300.219(b)(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public policy nondiscrimination requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a public policy requirement of HHS that no person otherwise eligible will be excluded from participation in, denied the benefits of, or otherwise subjected to discrimination in the administration of HHS programs, activities, projects, assistance, and services, to the extent doing so is prohibited by Federal statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement is in addition to 2 CFR 200.300(a) and applies as a public policy mandate for HHS award administration (§300.300(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to follow applicable Supreme Court decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS will follow all applicable Supreme Court decisions in administering its award programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an express obligation placed on HHS in administering awards (§300.300(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of sex discrimination provisions to include sexual orientation and gender identity
rubrics_metrics.description: In statutes administered by HHS that prohibit discrimination on the basis of sex, the Department interprets those provisions to include a prohibition against discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation and gender identity, consistent with Bostock v. Clayton County and related precedent; this provision is interpretive and does not impose substantive obligations on entities outside the Department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists the specific statutory authorities interpreted in paragraph (c)(1)–(13); the paragraph is expressly interpretive (§300.300(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Religious freedom and conscience protections - reliance
rubrics_metrics.description: A grant applicant or recipient may rely on applicable Federal protections for religious freedom and conscience; application of a particular provision(s) of this section shall not be required where such protections apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes eligibility to seek assurances/exemptions based on religious freedom or conscience protections (§300.300(d)(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification content for religious freedom/conscience assurance requests
rubrics_metrics.description: A notification seeking assurance must include: (i) the particular provision(s) from which the applicant/recipient asserts they are exempt; (ii) the legal basis supporting the exemption, including governing standards and statutory/Amendment/RFRA citations; and (iii) the factual basis identifying the conflict between religious/conscience beliefs and the requirements, including specific contexts, procedures, or services at issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification may be submitted at any time, before or during an investigation, to the HHS awarding agency, ASFR, or OCR (§300.300(d)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary exemption upon notification
rubrics_metrics.description: A temporary exemption from administrative investigation and enforcement will take effect upon the applicant's or recipient's submission of the notification; the temporary exemption is limited to the application of the particular provision(s) as applied to the specific contexts, procedures, or services identified in the notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If notification is received before an investigation, OCR/ASFR/HHS awarding agency must acknowledge receipt by email within 30 days and then work expeditiously to reach a determination; if during an investigation, the temporary exemption applies during the pendency of review (§300.300(d)(3)–(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination, written assurance, and appeal for exemption requests
rubrics_metrics.description: If HHS awarding agency/ASFR/OCR determines to provide assurance of exemption or modified application, the determination will be provided in writing and, if granted, exempts the applicant/recipient from OCR's administrative investigation and enforcement as applied to the specified provision(s) and contexts; an adverse determination may be appealed under the administrative procedures in 45 CFR part 81.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The temporary exemption will expire upon a final decision under 45 CFR part 81; determinations are not final for judicial review until after final decision under 45 CFR part 81 (§300.300(d)(4)–(6)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Severability of invalid or unenforceable provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Any provision of this section held to be invalid or unenforceable by its terms, or as applied to any person or circumstance, shall be severable from this section and shall not affect the remainder thereof or the application of the provision to other persons or circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard severability clause to preserve remainder of section (§300.300(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal payment and CMIA requirements for States
rubrics_metrics.description: For States, payments are governed by Treasury-State Cash Management Improvement Act (CMIA) agreements and default procedures codified at 31 CFR part 205 and TFM 4A-2000; to the extent CMIA agreements/default procedures do not address expenditure of program income, rebates, refunds, contract settlements, audit recoveries and interest, such funds must be expended before requesting additional cash payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This supplements 2 CFR 200.305(b) with HHS-specific payment ordering rules for States (§300.305(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval required for inclusion of research patient care costs
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient or subrecipient must request approval from the Federal agency or pass-through entity for the inclusion of research patient care costs in research awards made for the performance of research work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement supplements 2 CFR 200.308(f) and makes inclusion of research patient care costs subject to prior approval (§300.308).

rubrics_metrics.name: Intangible property - inventions under educational funding agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: No scholarship, fellowship, training grant, or other funding agreement made primarily to a recipient for educational purposes will contain any provision giving the Federal agency rights to inventions made by the recipient or subrecipient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This supplements 2 CFR 200.315(c) to protect invention rights for primarily educational awards (§300.315).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific indirect cost provisions for HHS
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional indirect cost provisions: (a) Indirect costs on training grants limited to a fixed rate of 8% of MTDC exclusive of tuition/related fees, equipment, and subawards > $25,000; (b) Indirect costs on grants to foreign organizations/public entities performed fully outside U.S. may be paid at a fixed 8% of MTDC with same exclusions; (c) Negotiated indirect costs may be paid to the American University, Beirut, and the World Health Organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are HHS-selected items of cost supplementing 2 CFR 200.414(c) (§300.414(a)–(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent research and development (IR&D) cost treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent research and development is R&D conducted by an organization not sponsored by Federal or non-Federal awards/contracts/agreements; IR&D shall be allocated its proportionate share of indirect costs on the same basis as sponsored R&D, but the cost of IR&D, including its proportionate share of indirect costs, is unallowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines IR&D and states unallowability of IR&D costs under HHS awards (§300.477).

rubrics_metrics.name: Shared responsibility payments unallowable
rubrics_metrics.description: Payments or assessments imposed on individuals pursuant to 26 U.S.C. 5000A(b) for failure to maintain minimum essential coverage prior to Jan 1, 2019, are not allowable; payments or assessments imposed on an employer pursuant to 26 U.S.C. 4980H for failure to offer minimum essential coverage to full-time employees (and dependents) are not allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the two types of shared responsibility payments that are unallowable expenses under Federal awards from an HHS awarding agency (§300.478(a)–(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of comments accepted under this IFR
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS will consider and address comments on HHS's plan and timeline for implementation, including provision of two effective dates, that are received within 30 days of the IFR publication; HHS will not respond to comments regarding OMB's 2020 or 2024 modifications to 2 CFR part 200 or on existing HHS-specific provisions merely being moved to 2 CFR part 300.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains comment scope because OMB amendments and already-finalized HHS provisions have been subject to prior public input; only implementation plan/timeline comments will be considered under this IFR preamble.
